result.note: Tests the US legal sequence on tariffs affecting India (Section 122 duty, the CIT ruling) and the Section 301 probe. The expected June negotiator visit is skipped as a forward-looking plan.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about US tariffs affecting India, as of May 2026:
items: After the US Supreme Court scrapped the "Liberation Day" tariffs, Washington imposed a 10% flat duty under Section 122.
The US Court of International Trade declared the 10% flat duties unlawful.
Following the US Court of International Trade ruling, US Customs stopped collecting the 10% duty from all importers.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because US Customs continues to collect the 10% duty from everyone except the specific plaintiffs, so the court win is narrow. The Supreme Court's removal of the Liberation Day tariffs knocked out the original basis for the India-US trade deal and stalled negotiations.
questions.source: US Customs continues to collect the tax from everyone except the specific plaintiffs.

questions.prompt: In 2026, after its "Liberation Day" tariffs were struck down, the United States opened investigations into Indian trade practices under which provision of US trade law?
questions.explain: Washington launched Section 301 investigations into Indian trade practices. Section 122 was the basis for the separate 10% flat duty. TBB notes that Section 301 action carries no expiry and no ceiling, which adds urgency to the trade talks.
questions.source: Washington pivoted to a 10% flat duty under Section 122 and launched Section 301 investigations into Indian trade practices
